preconditions.expression: all(line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip())
preconditions.description: All input lines are non-empty strings.
The first line contains exactly two integers n and q (1 ≤ n ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ q ≤ 10^5), followed by exactly q query lines.
The depth of the tree n and the number of queries q are within the given constraints.

preconditions.expression: all(line.split()[0] in ['1', '2'] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each query line starts with either '1' (operation) or '2' (edge count request).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 4 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.split()[0] == '1')
preconditions.description: For operation queries ('1 x'), x is an integer between 1 and 4 (inclusive).

postconditions.expression: all(line.strip() == '' or (line.split()[0] == '2' and len(line.split()) == 1) for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip())
postconditions.description: Each output line is either empty or a single integer (result of a '2' query).

postconditions.expression: all(int(line) >= 0 and int(line) < 1000000007 for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip())
postconditions.description: Each output line (result of a '2' query) is a non-negative integer modulo 1000000007.
The number of output lines equals the number of '2' queries in the input.

postconditions.expression: all(edges_after_operations[i] == int(stdout.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(num_queries_of_type_2))
postconditions.description: For each '2' query at position i, the output line is the number of edges in the graph after all preceding operations, modulo 1000000007. Here, edges_after_operations[i] is the correct edge count derived from the sequence of operations up to that query.
